es: Escribir un párrafo académico sobre hábitos de estudio con una afirmación clara, evidencia concreta sin matizar y una conclusión matizada con tres recursos de cautela de tipos distintos.

teaching.en: A good paragraph opens with a clear claim and supports it with concrete evidence, such as a substantial difference in scores, before it ends with a cautious conclusion.
teaching.es: Un buen párrafo abre con una afirmación clara y la apoya con pruebas concretas, como una diferencia considerable en las notas, antes de terminar con una conclusión cautelosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Tres partes: afirmación, evidencia y conclusión. Substantial describe una diferencia grande; cautious no significa dudar, sino decir solo lo que permiten los datos.
segments: A good paragraph opens with a clear claim and supports it with concrete evidence,
such as a substantial difference in scores, before it ends with a cautious conclusion.
teaching.audioText: A good paragraph opens with a clear claim and supports it with concrete evidence, such as a substantial difference in scores, before it ends with a cautious conclusion.

teaching.en: A short study session every day may be more effective than one long night of cramming, which students rarely enjoy.
teaching.es: Una sesión de estudio corta cada día puede ser más eficaz que una noche larga de estudio a última hora, que los estudiantes rara vez disfrutan.
teaching.explanationEs: La afirmación lleva un modal (may). Cramming es estudiar de golpe justo antes del examen.

than one long night of cramming, which students rarely enjoy.

teaching.en: A survey suggests that students who review their notes regularly retain more information, although the effect may depend on the subject.
teaching.es: Una encuesta sugiere que los estudiantes que repasan sus apuntes con regularidad retienen más información, aunque el efecto puede depender de la asignatura.
teaching.explanationEs: Retain es conservar en la memoria; depend on introduce un factor del que depende el resultado.
segments: A survey suggests that students who review their notes regularly retain
more information, although the effect may depend on the subject.

teaching.en: In the long run, a steady schedule is likely to work better than last-minute effort, although most of the evidence comes from what students say themselves.
teaching.es: A la larga, un horario constante probablemente funciona mejor que el esfuerzo de última hora, aunque la mayor parte de la evidencia procede de lo que dicen los propios estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: In the long run sitúa la conclusión en el tiempo; is likely to + verbo base expresa probabilidad. La reserva final admite el límite de los datos.
segments: In the long run, a steady schedule is likely to work better than
last-minute effort, although most of the evidence comes from what students say themselves.

teaching.en: To qualify a claim, choose one hedge of each kind: a verb such as suggest, a modal such as may, and an expression such as to a certain extent.
teaching.es: Para matizar una afirmación, elige un recurso de cada tipo: un verbo como suggest, un modal como may y una expresión como to a certain extent.
teaching.explanationEs: Qualify a claim es limitarla para que no diga más de lo que permiten las pruebas. Un recurso de cada tipo basta.
segments: To qualify a claim, choose one hedge of each kind: a verb such as suggest,
a modal such as may, and an expression such as to a certain extent.
teaching.audioText: To qualify a claim, choose one hedge of each kind: a verb such as suggest, a modal such as may, and an expression such as to a certain extent.

teaching.en: Keep the cautious language for the interpretation: a figure such as 200 students is plain fact, and only what it means needs hedging.
teaching.es: Reserva el lenguaje cauteloso para la interpretación: una cifra como 200 estudiantes es un hecho simple, y solo lo que significa necesita matiz.
teaching.explanationEs: No matices los datos, matiza lo que concluyes de ellos: así el párrafo suena preciso y no vacilante.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que abre el párrafo con una afirmación clara y cautelosa.

choices.text: Short daily study sessions may be more effective than one long night of study.
Everyone knows that studying every single night is the only way to pass exams.
It is possible that perhaps maybe studying might be somewhat better sometimes.

feedback.es: Una sola afirmación con un modal (may) es clara y prudente; la segunda exagera con everyone y only, y la tercera apila tantos matices que no dice nada.

hint.es: Busca una afirmación con un solo recurso de cautela, ni exagerada ni vacía.

origin.text: Mia is starting a paragraph about study habits. She wants one clear claim that does not say more than a small survey allows.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una sesión corta cada día puede ser más eficaz que una noche larga.»

feedback.es: Effective es el adjetivo que compara la eficacia de dos hábitos; el modal may deja la afirmación prudente.

origin.text: A short session every day may be more ___ than one long night before the exam, but the survey is small.

choices.text: It states the claim in the most cautious way possible.
It gives the evidence, stating the figure plainly.
It softens the conclusion with an expression of doubt.

feedback.es: La frase de la encuesta aporta la evidencia con una cifra concreta y sin matizar; los recursos de cautela aparecen en la afirmación y en la conclusión.

origin.audio: A good paragraph about study habits might begin like this: short daily study sessions may be more effective than one long night of cramming. A survey of two hundred students found that those who reviewed their notes regularly scored ten percent higher in the final exam. This suggests that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. To a certain extent, then, a steady schedule matters more than the number of hours.

origin.text: According to the survey, students who review their notes ___ tend to retain more, although the effect may vary from one subject to another.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo sobre hábitos de estudio con cautela.

answer.text: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.
accepted: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.

Some people think that listening to music while studying improves concentration. However, a study of 120 teenagers suggests that silence may be better for difficult tasks. The teenagers who worked in a quiet room scored eight percent higher on a reading test than those who listened to music. This seems to indicate that music can distract students, although it might help with simple tasks such as copying notes. It could be argued that some students are used to music and feel calmer with it, so the effect may depend on the person. Largely for this reason, the results should be read with care. Nevertheless, there is some evidence that a quiet schedule with short sessions is likely to work better for most students, but the sample was small and more research is needed before we can be sure of it.

feedback.es: Un buen párrafo abre con una afirmación clara, aporta una cifra concreta como evidencia y cierra con una conclusión con al menos tres recursos de cautela de tipos distintos.

origin.text: Escribe en inglés un párrafo de 190 a 240 palabras sobre hábitos de estudio. Incluye una afirmación clara, evidencia concreta (una cifra o un estudio inventado) y tres recursos de cautela de tipos distintos (un verbo como suggest, un modal como may y una expresión como to a certain extent). Termina con una conclusión matizada.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario de la profesora. ¿Qué corrige en la última frase de Leo?

choices.text: It hides the figure that the survey found, so it needs more detail.
It repeats the claim from the start, so it needs to be removed.
It overstates what the survey can show, so it needs softer wording.

feedback.es: La profesora propone cambiar prove por suggest y everyone por most students: la frase afirma más de lo que permite la encuesta y debe suavizarse.

origin.audio: After reading Leo's paragraph, the teacher said that the first half was strong: the claim was clear, and the survey figure was stated plainly. The problem came in the last sentence, where Leo wrote that the results prove that daily study works for everyone. She suggested replacing prove with suggest, and everyone with most students, and adding an expression such as to a certain extent.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión corrige mejor la primera frase del borrador de Leo?

choices.text: The survey suggests that short sessions may work better for many students.
Perhaps the survey might possibly suggest that short sessions may work a little.
The survey shows that short sessions work better for most of the students.

feedback.es: Sustituye proves por un verbo de cautela, añade un modal y cambia everyone por many students; las otras opciones apilan matices o siguen afirmando sin reserva.

origin.text: Leo's first draft reads: «The survey proves that short sessions work better for everyone. Fifty students improved their scores by ten percent.»

prompt.es: Completa: «El efecto puede depender de la asignatura.»

feedback.es: Depend on introduce el factor del que depende el resultado; con may la frase queda cautelosa.

origin.text: Daily review helped students in languages and science, but not in art. The effect may ___ on the subject, so the writer avoids absolute words.

prompt.es: Lee el párrafo de Sara. ¿Qué oración no necesita cautela y por qué?

choices.text: Sentence 2, because it already contains the main finding of the whole paragraph.
Sentence 1, because it reports a plain fact that can be checked.
Sentence 3, because it comes at the end of the paragraph.

feedback.es: Una cifra y una fecha son datos comprobables: se dicen sin matiz. La cautela se reserva para lo que significan los resultados.

origin.text: Sara's paragraph: (1) A survey of 200 students was carried out in March. (2) The results may suggest that students who sleep more tend to score higher. (3) It could be argued that the survey might possibly indicate a slight relationship.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Qué da a entender el narrador sobre la experiencia de su amigo?

choices.text: That the friend has studied the subject more than most people.
That research on students is always wrong about exams and study habits.
That it is a personal case that cannot prove a general rule.

feedback.es: El narrador contrapone tres exámenes de una sola persona a una investigación con muchos estudiantes: una experiencia personal no demuestra una regla general.

origin.audio: My friend says that cramming always works because he passed three exams that way. I told him that three exams are only a small sample of his own experience, and that research on many students points the other way. He laughed and said that research is one thing, but his results are another.

prompt.es: Completa: «Matizar una afirmación es limitarla a lo que permiten las pruebas.»

feedback.es: Qualify a claim es matizarla: añadir un verbo, un modal o una expresión que limite su alcance.

origin.text: To ___ a claim means to limit it, so that it says no more than the evidence allows.
